sources.label: Patches for YouTube VR (Meta Quest / Horizon OS), for use with Morphe
sources.author: YouTube VR
patch_list: Changes the app name shown in the headset's library and in app info. The stock name is just "YouTube", which is easy to confuse with the store app.

Starts every video at one resolution instead of the app's per-video choice; a resolution the video lacks falls back to its highest available (8K included when the stream spoof provides it). Changeable in the headset's Patch settings; Auto…
Injects the extension the other patches run through: its streaming spoof is what removes the pre-roll (ad-free playback) and provides the 8K format support. Turning this patch off restores ads.
Hides video ads, including the pre-roll when the streaming spoof is unavailable and the app falls back to its own player response.

Installs the patched app as a separate app by default, so it sits alongside the store's YouTube VR instead of replacing it. Replace mode keeps the official package name: the store copy has to be removed to satisfy the signing difference, H…
Builds the in-headset "Patch settings" hub and the SponsorBlock settings screen. The resource half of the SponsorBlock patch, which mines what this patch restructures the XML with.

Adds the in-headset switch for QUIC, the transport under HTTP/3: TLS over UDP, used for this app's API and media requests. Leave it on unless playback stalls on a network that blocks or throttles UDP 443 (corporate Wi-Fi, many VPNs), where…
Removes the dialog that appears when opening a video that has been age-restricted by accepting it automatically. This does not bypass the age restriction.
Automatically skips SponsorBlock segments (sponsors, self-promos, intros, ...). On by default (sponsors: skip once); configure per-category behaviour below or in the headset's Patch settings screen.
Adds an option to trick the app into thinking you are running a different version; the option ships set to the app's current version, so selecting the patch alone changes nothing.
Adds an option to report a different app package name in the Cronet User-Agent; the option ships set to the original package name, so selecting the patch alone changes nothing.

sources.label: Morphe patches for YouTube VR (Meta Quest)
sources.author: YouTube VR
patch_list: Adds an option to disable QUIC (Quick UDP Internet Connections) network protocol.
Allows the app to work without root by using a different package name when patched using a GmsCore instead of Google Play Services.
Opens links in an external app instead of the in-app browser.
Removes the dialog that appears when opening a video that has been age-restricted by accepting it automatically. This does not bypass the age restriction.
Adds an option to trick the app into thinking you are running a different version.
